ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the circuit there are upper and lower two-input threshold/OR function blocks, and both blocks are marked with “≥1”. The two inputs of the upper block are respectively labeled A and B; the two inputs of the lower block are respectively labeled C and D. The output terminals of the two function blocks are connected to the same vertical node, which is labeled to the right as output Y, and this node is pulled up to +Vcc through resistor R. Reasoning: A two-input block marked with “≥1” means that as long as any one input is 1, the output condition is satisfied; therefore the upper block output X1 = A + B, and the lower block output X2 = C + D. Since the two outputs are connected on the same common node with a pull-up resistor, this connection implements a wired-AND relationship, so the common output Y = X1·X2. Substituting gives Y = (A + B)(C + D).

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: two two-input threshold/OR blocks feed a shared output node Y, and that node is pulled up to +Vcc through R. Compute the upper block output as X1 = A + B and the lower block output as X2 = C + D. Because the two outputs are connected together with a pull-up, the shared node implements X1 AND X2. Therefore write Y = X1·X2 = (A + B)(C + D).
